thread:
Maria G: Quick sync — I'm drafting a compact SEV routing + war-room pattern for partners (cloud marketplaces, HW vendors, SI). Want a short, actionable playbook we can share with partners and link in partner agreements. Thoughts?
Sam K: +1. Can we keep it to a 3-step runbook? Trigger -> War room -> Handoff.
Devon L: Agreed. Also need naming convention for shared channels, e.g. #partner-<org>-sev or #partner-<org>-ops. Keeps things searchable.
Alex R: One ask from infra: include a fallback model routing rule (hosted -> dedicated -> private) so partners know expected latency/policy changes when we fallback.
Maria G: Good call. Also include who owns what at each step (Redwood oncall, partner SRE, partner TAM, Redwood AE).
Sam K: Draft suggestion for channel names: 
• #partner-<org>-sev — primary war room when partner is involved
• #partner-<org>-ops — ongoing operational syncs after SEV
• @redwood-oncall — used for pages in SEV1/SEV2
Kevin (partner-bizops-bot): FYI: marketplace partners asked for a single point-of-contact matrix last week. If we add an attached CSV to the playbook that'd help.
Devon L: I'll prep a CSV template. Fields: partner, TAM, SRE pager, escalation tier, business-hours contact, off-hours pager.
Maria G: Example minimal playbook (put this in the doc & as pinned message in the shared channel):
```
1) Trigger: partner reports customer-impacting issue OR Redwood detects degradations affecting partner routes.
2) Triage (first 10m): post in #partner-<org>-sev, tag @redwood-oncall and partner SRE, paste short symptom + affected models/routes.
3) War room (if >10m or high-impact): run /warroom create "Partner <org> SEV" --severity=SEV2 --participants="@redwood-oncall, partner-sre, partner-tam, ae"
4) Roles: Incident Lead (Redwood) — coordinates triage, Partner Lead — provides partner context, Tech Owner(s) — root cause.
5) Escalation ladder: SEV3 -> Slack thread; SEV2 -> War room; SEV1 -> Pager + Exec notify.
6) Handoff: use the handback template (summary, RCA link, follow-ups, owner).
```
Sam K: Small UX note: include a canned message template for the initial post so partners don't forget context. Something like:
"<short summary> — impact, affected customers, last good time, immediate mitigation tried"
Alex R: We should add automated tooling hooks: when /warroom create runs, incident-bot should auto-pin the runbook link and create a temporary #partner-<org>-sev-YYYY channel.
incident-bot: action: created incident 1718123456-PARTNER-ORG. Pinned: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/partner-sev
Devon L: Onboard checklist for partner SREs: confirm pager subscription, verify contact CSV, check read-only access to metrics dashboards, and confirm runbook receipt.
Maria G: Question for partnerships team: do we allow partners to invite their own L2s into the Redwood oncall channel or do we require all partner personnel use the partner-specific channel?
Sam K: Prefer partner-specific channel for audit + compliance. We can create short-lifetime cross-org channels for War room only and log membership.
Kevin (partner-bizops-bot): We'll add a short compliance clause to the partner onboarding checklist: "All SEV traffic must occur in designated partner channels; cross-org channels are ephemeral and logged."
Alex R: One more: include expected SLAs for response windows in the playbook (e.g., initial ack within 15m for SEV2, mitigation plan within 1h).
Maria G: Nice. Devon — can you assemble a 1-page PDF + runbook link? I'll share with the top 10 partners for feedback.
Devon L: Yep, will have a draft CSV + 1-pager by EOD tomorrow.
Sam K: I'll add the fallback routing snippet and a quick note on telemetry ownership.
Maria G: Perfect. Thanks team. I'll loop in legal for the minor clause change once draft is ready.
Kevin (partner-bizops-bot): Reminder: marketplace partner summit next Wed — we can workshop the playbook there. :calendar:
Alex R: If we test one partner now (small HW vendor), we can refine before summit.
Maria G: Let's do that. Kickoff with vendor next Tue 14:00 PT. I'll create the invite. :thumbsup:
